metaTitle: Best Extra Sticky Lint Rollers in 2026
metaDescription: Five extra sticky lint roller sets compared by sheet count, refills, tear design and handle style, from a 1110 sheet bulk kit to a simple two pack.
introParagraphs: Extra sticky lint rollers are for the jobs a standard roller gives up on: a dog that sheds on every dark sweater, a cat that sleeps on the good armchair, a wool coat that attracts everything. The stronger adhesive helps, but it only matters if the roll has enough sheets, tears cleanly and fits your hand. We compared five extra sticky options that differ mainly in how they are packaged.

The spread of supply is large. The MEIQIHOME is a mega set with 1110 sheets and five handles, the Swihauk and Beitophome each provide 600 sheets with spiral or perforated tear designs, and the Scotch-Brite pet pack gives four sealed rollers with 192 sheets total. The Evercare is the simplest, with two rollers of 100 sheets each and a comfort grip.

We evaluated each pick based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at sheet supply, refill structure, tear design and handle comfort. The sections below explain how to pick between a bulk kit and a ready to use pack, instead of simply ranking by number of sheets.

products.name: Beitophome 600 Sheet Extra Sticky Lint Roller Kit

specList.label: Adhesive
specList.value: High tack for pet hair and lint

products.description:
The Beitophome is the most balanced kit in this guide. You get 600 sheets, with two rollers already loaded and four refills in the box, at 100 sheets per roll. That means you can keep one roller upstairs and one downstairs and still have months of supply left in refills.

The high tack adhesive sheets are described as grabbing dog hair, cat fur, lint and dust from clothes, couches and car seats in one pass. Every roll is pre scored with high contrast tear lines, which helps anyone who has trouble finding the end of a sticky sheet. The tradeoff is that swapping a refill needs some grip strength, and spare rolls need dry storage until you use them.

Setup is as simple as using the pre loaded rollers, and cleaning is not needed. Compared with the MEIQIHOME, you get a smaller supply but a simpler box. Against the Swihauk, you get two handles loaded and four refills rather than six sealed style rolls and two handles.
products.bestFor: Most pet homes that want months of supply
pros: 600 sheets cover months of regular use
Two rollers loaded so one can live upstairs
High contrast tear lines are easy to find
100 sheets per roll
cons: Refill swap needs some grip strength

products.name: MEIQIHOME 1110 Sheet Extra Sticky Lint Roller Set
products.description:
The MEIQIHOME is the choice for a big household or a heavy shedder. It is a mega value set with 1110 sheets and five handles, plus a pile of refill rolls, so you can station a roller in every room and in the car. The extra sticky adhesive suits pet hair on clothes and larger surfaces.

The listing frames the set as a bulk saving, and the scale is the selling point. One box can last a year or more for most homes. The tradeoff is storage, because a bulk box needs real space, and it is far more supply than a one person, pet free home will ever use.

Setup involves loading a roll onto each handle, and cleaning is not needed. Compared with the Beitophome, you get nearly double the sheets and more handles but a bulkier box. Against the Scotch-Brite pack, you trade ready to use sealed rollers for a refill system that creates less waste.
products.bestFor: Big households and heavy shedding pets
pros: 1110 sheets last a year or more for most homes
Five handles to station around the house
Extra sticky adhesive suits pet hair
Refill rolls cut waste
cons: Bulk box needs real storage space
Too much supply for a pet free single home

products.name: Swihauk 600 Sheet Extra Sticky Lint Rollers
products.description:
The Swihauk packs 600 sheets across six rollers, with two ergonomic handles to move between rooms. The easy spiral tear design lets sheets come off the roll cleanly one by one, which avoids the frustration of tearing two layers at once. The listing describes an extra sticky formula for pet hair, dust and debris.

Six separate rollers give you flexibility, because you can load a fresh one without waiting for the old one to finish. The tradeoff is that seating a new roller takes some thumb pressure, and a hand roller still needs bending for low spots. With only two handles, you will be swapping rolls between rooms rather than keeping one everywhere.

Setup is loading a roller on a handle, and there is no cleaning. Compared with the Beitophome, you get the same 600 sheets but more individual rollers and fewer handles. Against the MEIQIHOME, you get a smaller supply with a spiral tear design.
products.bestFor: People who want clean one sheet tearing
pros: 600 sheets across six rollers
Spiral tear sheets peel one at a time
Two ergonomic handles for different rooms
Extra sticky formula for pet hair
cons: Seating a new roller takes thumb pressure
Still requires bending for low spots

products.name: Scotch-Brite Pet Extra Sticky Lint Rollers, 4 Pack
products.description:
The Scotch-Brite pet pack is the no fuss option. Four ready to use rollers with 48 sheets each give you 192 sheets in total, and nothing needs loading. The surface is described as extra sticky and 50 percent stickier, designed to pick up lint, hair and debris without damaging clothes or fabrics.

It works on clothes, couches, curtains, car seats and lamp shades, and the maker positions it as a replacement for hauling out the vacuum. The tradeoff is the modest supply, since 192 sheets is used up fast with pets, and the sealed rollers cannot be refilled, so there is more waste. It is better for light shedding than a heavy shedder.

There is no setup beyond peeling a sheet, and the rollers are disposable. Compared with the Beitophome, you get a smaller supply but no refill handling. Against the Evercare, you get four rollers instead of two, but fewer sheets per roller.
products.bestFor: Light shedding where nothing should need loading
pros: Four ready rollers, no refill loading needed
Extra sticky surface suits pet hair
Works on clothes, couches and curtains
Trusted brand and familiar handle
cons: Only 192 sheets total, used up fast with pets

products.name: Evercare Pet Hair Lint Rollers, 2 Pack
products.description:
The Evercare is the simplest extra sticky pack. It includes two ultra sticky rollers with 100 sheets each, so you get 200 sheets in total. Precision razor cut edges make the sheets tear cleanly, and a contoured grip handle makes it comfortable for both quick touch ups and larger projects.

The listing describes it as effective on dog hair, cat fur and lint on clothes and furniture. The easy tear design helps anyone who gets frustrated by sheets that peel unevenly. The tradeoff is the limited supply, because 200 sheets across two rollers runs out quickly, and the adhesive tires on heavy fur.

There is nothing to set up, and the rollers are ready to use. Compared with the Scotch-Brite pack, you get fewer rollers but more sheets per roller. Against the Beitophome, you get a smaller supply and no refill system, but a lower cost and zero loading.
products.bestFor: Light to moderate shedding with minimal fuss
pros: Two rollers with 100 sheets each
Razor cut edges tear cleanly
Contoured grip suits longer jobs
No loading needed
cons: Adhesive tires quickly on heavy fur

buyingCriteria.explanation: Rolls typically carry 56 to 120 sheets, so a pack can look generous and still run out. The MEIQIHOME offers 1110 sheets, the Beitophome and Swihauk 600 each, the Scotch-Brite pack 192 and the Evercare 200. Compare the price per sheet rather than the pack size, since multi packs are often cheaper per sheet. If you have a shedding pet, supply matters more than any other number.

Extra sticky is a manufacturer claim, such as the Scotch-Brite pet pack's 50 percent stickier. It helps with fur but can tug on delicate knits and silk. Adhesive also loses tack after a few passes over heavy hair, so peel a fresh sheet often. Test a hidden area on delicate clothes.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Decide between refills and sealed rollers
buyingCriteria.explanation: Refill systems like the MEIQIHOME, Beitophome and Swihauk reduce waste, but you must load rolls onto handles. Sealed rollers like the Scotch-Brite and Evercare are ready to use but create more waste. Confirm that any refill fits your handle. If waste matters, refills are the better choice.

A clean tear saves time and frustration. The Swihauk uses a spiral tear, the Beitophome uses high contrast perforated lines, and the Evercare has razor cut edges. Clear tear lines help anyone who struggles to find the edge of a sheet. Test the tear on your first sheet.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Think about handle comfort and reach
buyingCriteria.explanation: A comfortable handle reduces hand fatigue and helps anyone with arthritic hands. The Swihauk has two ergonomic handles and the Evercare a contoured grip. Standard rollers are about 4 inches wide, while jumbo versions near 6.5 inches cover clothing faster. Choose the handle that fits your hand.

A 1110 sheet kit like the MEIQIHOME takes real space, and spare refills need dry storage. A small household may prefer the Evercare pair. Keep refills sealed in a dry cabinet. Match the box size to the room you have.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sheet supply and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted sheets, rollers and refills in each kit, from the MEIQIHOME's 1110 to the Scotch-Brite pack's 192. We looked at how long each supply would last in a typical home. Total value mattered.

howWeEvaluated.title: Adhesive claims
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed the extra sticky claims, such as the Scotch-Brite pack's 50 percent stickier and the Evercare's ultra sticky description. We noted which claims were quantified. Fabric safety was also considered.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tear design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared spiral tear, perforated lines and razor cut edges. The Swihauk and Beitophome offered the clearest designs. Clean tearing mattered for ease of use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handle and refill system
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed handle comfort and the refill approach of each kit. The Swihauk's ergonomic handles and the MEIQIHOME's five handles stood out. Ready to use rollers scored for simplicity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Strongest versus most basic pick
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the Beitophome, with its 600 sheets, loaded rollers and clear tear lines, against the Evercare, a simple two pack with 200 sheets. The Beitophome earns Best Overall for balance, while the Evercare suits light needs. Value and convenience were weighed alongside the feature gap.

cards.label: Refillable kits
cards.text: The MEIQIHOME, Beitophome and Swihauk give a large supply with handles and refills, which cuts waste. They need loading and storage. Choose these for pet homes.

cards.label: Ready-to-use rollers
cards.text: The Scotch-Brite and Evercare packs arrive loaded and need no handling. They run out faster and create more waste. Recommendation: pick refills for heavy shedding, and ready to use rollers for light needs.

cards.text: A large supply, strong adhesive and clean tearing, since pet hair uses sheets quickly. Spare refills should be easy to store.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Beitophome suits best, with 600 sheets and two loaded rollers. The MEIQIHOME is the alternative for a very large supply.

cards.label: Spend more if

faq.q: How do I choose between a bulk kit and a ready-to-use pack?
faq.a: A bulk kit like the MEIQIHOME or Beitophome gives a large supply and reduces waste with refills, but needs loading and storage. A ready to use pack like the Scotch-Brite or Evercare is simple but runs out faster. If you have pets, choose a kit, and for light needs a ready to use pack is enough.

They range from the lowest-cost Evercare to the premium MEIQIHOME. Bulk kits cost more up front but are often cheaper per sheet. Check the current price on Amazon before deciding, since it changes often.

faq.q: Will extra sticky rollers damage clothes?
faq.a: They can tug on delicate knits and silk, so test a hidden area first and use light pressure. Sturdy cotton and wool are generally fine. If a fabric feels at risk, use a standard adhesive roller instead.
It depends on shedding. For a home with one pet, 600 sheets from the Beitophome or Swihauk can last several months. A heavy shedder uses more, so the MEIQIHOME's 1110 sheets is a safer bet.

faq.q: Do extra sticky rollers work on furniture?
faq.a: Yes, the Scotch-Brite and Evercare listings mention couches, curtains and car seats. Standard rollers are about 4 inches wide, so large furniture takes many passes. A wider roller covers more per pass.

faq.q: How should I store spare refills?
faq.a: Keep them in a dry cabinet in their packaging until needed. Moisture and dust reduce adhesive tack. The Beitophome and MEIQIHOME refills should stay sealed until you load them.
